pattern_id: Trim-before-execute GC race skipping committed instances
description:
In efficient-epaxos, the Exec engine uses ExecedUpTo[q] as a lower bound when scanning dependency ranges in strongconnect:

  for q := 0; q < N; q++ {
      inst := v.Deps[q]
      for i := ExecedUpTo[q] + 1; i <= inst; i++ {
          ... wait for InstanceSpace[q][i] to become non-nil/COMMITTED ...
      }
  }

It never inspects or re-validates instances at indices <= ExecedUpTo[q]; it assumes any such instances have already been executed locally. If a separate GC/truncation component advances ExecedUpTo[q] and/or deletes InstanceSpace[q][i] based solely on *remote* watermarks (minExecutedUpTo/minCommittedUpTo) without first ensuring that the local instance (q,i) is actually EXECUTED, then after a crash+restart the replica can be in a state where:

  - Some instance I = (q,i) was COMMITTED but never EXECUTED locally.
  - On crash-restart, GC metadata persists (ExecedUpTo[q] >= i), but the in-memory record for I has been trimmed (InstanceSpace[q][i] == nil) and I.Status is lost.
  - Another instance J (possibly on a different leader) has Deps[q] = i and is COMMITTED.

When executeCommand is invoked on J, strongconnect will skip the entire range [0..i] for replica q because deps[q] == i <= ExecedUpTo[q]; the inner loop "for i := ExecedUpTo[q]+1; i <= deps[q]; i++" is empty. As a result, Exec treats dependency I as already satisfied even though it never executed it locally, and proceeds to execute J. This silently drops I's effect on the local state while allowing later dependent commands to execute, violating safety (state-machine consistency and per-instance execution invariants) without any error or recovery attempt.

The trim_before_execute_race_test.go test constructs this post-crash, post-GC in-memory state directly using an UnknownDepReplica, installs a critical command C1 at (R1,0) and a dependent command C2 at (R2,0) with Deps[1] = 0, then:
  - Marks C1 as only COMMITTED (never EXECUTED),
  - Forces victim.ExecedUpTo[1] = 0 and deletes InstanceSpace[1][0] to simulate GC+crash-restart,
  - Calls executeCommand on C2.
The current Exec implementation returns true and marks C2 EXECUTED even though C1 is absent and was never executed on that replica, demonstrating the vulnerability pattern.

The current repository does not implement production GC or persistent crash-restart, so the concrete state is unreachable today, but any future GC layer that persists ExecedUpTo or trims logs without strictly coupling it to local EXECUTED status will be vulnerable in exactly this way.
trigger_condition: At some replica Rv, after GC+crash-restart: (1) there exists an instance I=(r,i) such that (a) I was COMMITTED but never EXECUTED locally before crash, (b) GC decided to trim I based on global watermarks and removed its log entry so InstanceSpace[r][i] == nil, and (c) GC persisted or recomputed ExecedUpTo[r] >= i; (2) there exists a dependent instance J such that J.Deps[r] == i and J is COMMITTED on Rv; (3) executeCommand is invoked on J at Rv. Under these conditions, strongconnect will skip the missing dependency range because deps[r] <= ExecedUpTo[r], and will execute J despite never executing I locally.
test_template:
1. Construct an in-memory EPaxos replica type that exposes InstanceSpace, ExecedUpTo and the real Exec engine (executeCommand). Reuse helpers like UnknownDepReplica/CrashReuseReplica.
2. Create a critical command C1 at some instance I=(r,i) and a later command C2 at instance J=(s,j) that explicitly depends on I via Deps[r] = i. Use conflicting operations on the same key so that missing C1 is semantically meaningful (e.g., two writes or increments on key x).
3. On a set of baseline replicas, deliver commits for C1 and C2 via handleCommit and drive execution normally (executeCommand on C2), then verify both instances become EXECUTED and the final state matches the expected ordering (C1 then C2).
4. On a designated victim replica, deliver Commit(C1) and Commit(C2) so that both are COMMITTED but not yet EXECUTED. Then simulate a buggy GC+crash-restart by:
   - Setting victim.ExecedUpTo[r] = i as if C1 had been executed,
   - Deleting victim.InstanceSpace[r][i] (and optionally clearing its status) to model trimming of I while losing EXECUTED metadata.
5. Verify that C2's dependency still points at I (Deps[r] == i).
6. Invoke victim.exec.executeCommand(s,j) in a background goroutine and wait for it to either complete or block. The vulnerability is present if executeCommand returns true and marks C2 EXECUTED even though InstanceSpace[r][i] == nil and I was never executed locally.
7. Optionally, assert that C1 remains non-EXECUTED on the victim and that no recovery logic is triggered for I, and compare final state or executed-command sets across replicas to show that the victim skipped C1 while executing later commands.
